definition.title: Healthy-adult resting supine pulmonary 0D reference candidate

baseline_cardiac_output.derivation: Six L/min is a prespecified nominal resting calibration value within the published 4-8 L/min normal interval and aligns with the dissertation whole-body rest baseline.

left_atrial_pressure.derivation: Eight mmHg is a prespecified nominal pressure-sink calibration value below the published PAWP upper limit of 15 mmHg; PAWP is used as a left-atrial pressure surrogate.

pulmonary_vascular_resistance.derivation: 1.2 Wood units is a prespecified nominal calibration value within the published 0.3-2.0 Wood-unit normal interval.

pulmonary_arterial_compliance.derivation: Five mL/mmHg is a prespecified nominal calibration value above the published normal lower limit of 2.3 mL/mmHg.

pulmonary_transit_time.derivation: Median right-to-left ventricular first-pass pulmonary transit time in 18 age- and sex-matched healthy controls; the reported 25th-75th percentile interval is retained.

right_lung_perfusion_fraction.derivation: Derived as RPA/(RPA+LPA) from supine mean indexed flows 1996 and 1592 mL/min/m2; one-SD bounds use first-order propagation of the reported SDs 274 and 266.

mean_pulmonary_arterial_pressure_target.derivation: The 15.2 mmHg equilibrium prediction equals left-atrial pressure plus cardiac output times PVR and is compared with the published 8-20 mmHg normal interval; this is a reference comparison, not independent subject-level validation.

validity.population: healthy adults represented by guideline normal ranges and small healthy-volunteer imaging cohorts
validity.physiological_state: resting and supine; steady mean-flow reference
validity.description: Two-element mean pulmonary Windkessel with a fixed left-atrial pressure sink, total pulmonary transit delay, and parallel right/left flow partition.

limitations: This is a research reference candidate, not a diagnostic or treatment model.
The model resolves mean pressure only and omits pulsatile ventricular and valve dynamics.
PAWP is used as a surrogate for left-atrial pressure and the nominal calibration values are not a jointly measured individual data set.
The total transit delay does not distinguish arterial, capillary, and venous residence times.
Right/left perfusion is aggregate; lobar, gravitational, ventilation-perfusion, and exercise redistribution are not represented.
The transit-time source uses right-to-left ventricular first-pass timing, so its measurement definition must remain attached to comparisons.
Gas exchange, biochemical exchange, capillary recruitment, autoregulation, disease, sex, age, and patient-specific anatomy are outside this version.
